tables.label: Sparse observations
tables.setting: 128 × 128 fields. 500 observations, or 1% near the cylinder for bounded NS.
tables.note: All errors in %. Darcy measures coefficient classification error. Other columns measure pixel-wise relative error. Baselines were trained on full observations.

details.Evaluation: 128 × 128 fields. Sparse setting: 500 solution/final-state observations for Darcy, Poisson, Helmholtz and non-bounded Navier–Stokes. Bounded Navier–Stokes uses 1% observations near the cylinder boundary. Evaluation averages 1,000 random scenes and observations.
details.Uncertainty: These tables give means. Do not invent uncertainties for baseline methods.
details.Interpretation: Darcy uses binary coefficient error rate. Other fields use mean pixel-wise relative error, not relative L2 error. Baseline networks are trained with full observations. Sparse-input testing therefore evaluates adaptation to missing inputs. Show this next to the sparse table. Full-observation results form a separate comparison. These are paper-reported results, not a reproduction or current universal ranking.

tables.label: Poisson · PInv
tables.setting: Poisson coefficient recovery on [0,1]². 2,500 noisy observations. 20,000 epochs, three runs.
tables.note: Solve time includes per-instance optimization. It is not a trained model’s forward-pass latency.

details.Setting: PInv on [0,1]^2. 2,500 solution observations on a 50 x 50 grid. Gaussian noise is written N(0,0.1) in the paper. Preserve that notation without inferring a standard-deviation convention.
details.Evaluation: Mean and standard deviation over three runs. 20,000 optimization epochs. The paper labels the error L2RE.
details.Cost definition: Table 14 gives the mean runtime for per-instance optimization. This is online solution cost, not reusable offline pretraining and not a single network forward pass.
details.Hardware: Section 4.1 reports a server with 20 Intel Xeon Silver 4210 CPUs and eight RTX 2080 Ti GPUs. Per-run GPU allocation is not specified. The paper describes 12 GB per GPU. This hardware description is retained as reported, not independently verified.
details.Selection: Vanilla PINN, boundary-weighted PINN, gradient-enhanced PINN, and the variational method labelled vPINN in the source.

details.Setting: HInv on [-1,1]^2 x [0,1]. 2,500 random space-time observations. Gaussian noise written N(0,0.1).
details.Evaluation: Same four method labels as PInv. Mean and standard deviation over three runs with 20,000 optimization epochs.
details.Selection: Retains the same method set as PInv to show task dependence, including unsuccessful high-error results.

tables.setting: Train on 64 × 64 single-airfoil flow. Evaluate one-airfoil designs at 128 × 128.

details.Evaluation: Appendix D.1: 10 batches, 20 candidates per batch. Select the best design in each batch, then average across 10 batches. Table 3 gives means without uncertainty intervals.

tables.label: Half-domain control
tables.setting: Outer-half observation, actuation, and evaluation. 50 test trajectories. A100 80 GB + 16 CPU cores.

metrics.label: Control objective J
metrics.definition: Time-space integral of squared tracking error over the observed outer halves.

metrics.label: Inference time
metrics.definition: Reported inference time under the Table 4 hardware and half-domain setting.

tables.note: Default diffusion: 900 steps. DDIM: 30 steps. J and inference time are reported together for this setting.

details.Protocol: This evaluates trajectory tracking on the outer half of the spatial domain. Do not merge with DiffPhyCon 2024 terminal-state PO-FC errors. The source reports means but no standard deviations in Table 4. Table 1's time is averaged across six settings. Prefer this Table 4 for a matched accuracy-versus-time chart. The source's 'inference time' should retain its label without inventing a batch size or per-step normalization.
details.Metric definitions: Control objective J: Time-space integral of squared tracking error over the observed outer halves. Inference time: Reported inference time under the Table 4 hardware and half-domain setting.

groups.title: SafeDiffCon
groups.subtitle: Safety-constrained smoke control
groups.summary: Delivery performance evaluated jointly with safety violations.

source.title: From Uncertain to Safe: Conformal Adaptation of Diffusion Models for Safe PDE Control

tables.label: 2D smoke
tables.setting: 128 × 128 smoke flow. Peripheral actuation toward a target exit. Hazardous-region smoke fraction capped at 0.1.

metrics.label: Control objective J
metrics.definition: Negative fraction of smoke reaching the target exit.

metrics.label: Unsafe trajectories
metrics.definition: Percentage of evaluated trajectories exceeding the safety bound.

tables.note: Read J together with safety. A lower objective with unsafe trajectories is not a better feasible controller. Zero unsafe trajectories describes this test set only.

details.Protocol: Never rank this safety-constrained task by the control objective alone. More negative unsafe baselines do not win the constrained task. Only SafeDiffCon reports zero unsafe trajectories in this table. This is finite-test evidence, not a universal safety guarantee. No standard deviations or matched inference times in Table 2. Retain SVM exactly as reported. The text defines it but does not specify an extra normalization in the table.
details.Metric definitions: Control objective J: Negative fraction of smoke reaching the target exit. Safety violation magnitude: Reported SVM, defined as max(s - 0.1, 0). Unsafe trajectories: Percentage of evaluated trajectories exceeding the safety bound.
